session.question: How does the theme of "Green Cluod Computing" connect the discussion of Green IoT with the systematic survey of energy-efficient techniques in sustainabl cloud computing, especially regarding why data centers and cloud technologies are being optimized for lower energy use and reduced environmental harm?
session.answer:
Green Cloud Computing (GCC) provides the common sustainability framework linking Green IoT and energy-efficient cloud computing. In both settings, the core objective is to reduce the power demand of connected computing systems and thereby lower CO2 emissions and broader environmental impacts. For Green IoT, this means conserving energy across massive device, edge, fog, and cloud layers; for cloud computing, it means improving the efficiency of data centers and workloads that support those IoT services. (alsharif2024acomprehensivesurvey chunk 1, bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)

The systematic survey shows that this optimization is driven by the large and growing energy footprint of data centers, computing devices, and networking infrastructure. These systems consume substantial electricity, generate significant heat, and contribute to carbon emissions, so the literature emphasizes techniques such as VM virtualization and consolidation, power-aware scheduling, task offloading, resource shutdown, thermal management, and learning-based control to reduce energy use while preserving service quality. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1, buyya2023energy‐efficiencyandsustainability chunk 1, mansour2022designofcultural chunk 1)

The Green IoT connection is that IoT deployments depend on cloud and edge infrastructure to process data efficiently. Therefore, optimizing cloud technologies is not only a data-center problem but also a prerequisite for sustainable IoT at scale. By making cloud data centers less energy-intensive and less carbon-intensive, GCC supports the sustainability goals of Green IoT and environmentally responsible computing more broadly. (alsharif2024acomprehensivesurvey chunk 1, wang2023reinforcementlearningbased chunk 1, buyya2023energy‐efficiencyandsustainability chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-69f97adc: The excerpt explains that rising energy use and CO2 emissions from data centers, computing devices, and network equipment contribute to global warming and other environmental harms. To address this, the paper surveys 119 studies on energy-efficient techniques in sustainable cloud computing, focusing on green cloud computing and the role of cloud data centers in reducing energy consumption and CO2 footprints. It highlights techniques such as VM virtualization and consolidation, power-aware methods, bio-inspired approaches, and thermal management. The survey notes that many researchers favor software-level solutions because they require less infrastructure and are less prone to failures. This connects to Green IoT by showing a shared goal: optimizing connected computing systems for lower power use and reduced environmental impact.
From Salil Bharany, Sandeep Sharma, Osamah Ibrahim Khalaf, Ghaida Muttashar Abdulsahib, Abeer S. Al Humaimeedy, Theyazn H. H. Aldhyani, Mashael Maashi, and Hasan Alkahtani. A systematic survey on energy-efficient techniques in sustainable cloud computing. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14106256, doi:10.3390/su14106256.

pqac-a92cab39: The excerpt explains that data centers consume a significant amount of energy and contribute heavily to global energy use and carbon emissions, making energy reduction a key sustainability goal. It introduces a federated cloud approach and a reinforcement learning framework (ERLFC) designed to schedule tasks across geographically distributed cloud data centers by considering energy consumption, cooling method, waiting time, energy type, emission ratio, and total energy use. The paper emphasizes that optimizing cloud infrastructure can lower both energy consumption and emissions, and reports simulation results showing improvements over baseline scheduling methods. This connects to Green Cloud Computing as a focus on making cloud technologies more energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable.
From Zhibao Wang, Shuaijun Chen, Lu Bai, Juntao Gao, Jinhua Tao, Raymond R. Bond, and Maurice Mulvenna. Reinforcement learning based task scheduling for environmentally sustainable federated cloud computing. Journal of Cloud Computing Advances Systems and Applications, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13677-023-00553-0, doi:10.1186/s13677-023-00553-0.

pqac-49d6861b: The excerpt is a 2024 survey on energy-efficient computing for sustainable massive IoT networks. It explains that IoT devices have limited computational power and energy resources, and that computing technologies such as edge, fog, and cloud can conserve energy by supporting data collection and processing. The survey claims to cover all types of green computing and discusses energy-saving techniques including energy-aware architecture, data aggregation and compression, low-power hardware, energy-aware scheduling, task offloading, turning off unused resources, virtualization, energy harvesting, and cooling optimization. It frames these approaches as a roadmap toward sustainable computing for massive IoT networks and environmentally friendly systems.
From Mohammed H. Alsharif, Anabi Hilary Kelechi, Abu Jahid, Raju Kannadasan, Manish Kumar Singla, Jyoti Gupta, and Zong Woo Geem. A comprehensive survey of energy-efficient computing to enable sustainable massive iot networks. Alexandria Engineering Journal, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aej.2024.01.067, doi:10.1016/j.aej.2024.01.067.

pqac-2276f15c: The excerpt discusses energy-efficiency and sustainability in new generation cloud computing, framing cloud data centers as a major global energy challenge. It notes that cloud services are increasingly important but consume vast amounts of electricity worldwide, with projections that data centers could use 20% of global electricity and emit up to 5.5% of carbon emissions by 2025. A large portion of this energy becomes heat, causing reliability, device lifetime, and cooling problems. The paper proposes a learning-centric approach for integrated management of cloud resources and workloads to reduce energy consumption and carbon footprint while maintaining service quality. This connects to Green Cloud Computing as the motivation for optimizing cloud infrastructures for lower energy use and less environmental impact.
From Rajkumar Buyya, Shashikant Ilager, and Patricia Arroba. Energy‐efficiency and sustainability in new generation cloud computing: a vision and directions for integrated management of data centre resources and workloads. Software Practice and Experience, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/spe.3248, doi:10.1002/spe.3248.

pqac-46477e17: The excerpt explains that Green Cloud Computing (GCC) addresses energy-related challenges caused by the growing size of data centers. It highlights that GCC aims to reduce energy utilization in cloud data centers through load balancing and optimized resource scheduling. The proposed CEPO-based method is designed to distribute workload across data centers to avoid overload, reduce operational and maintenance costs, and lower both energy use and heat generation. This connects to the broader theme of energy-efficient techniques in sustainable cloud computing by showing why cloud infrastructures are being optimized: to improve performance while minimizing energy consumption and environmental impact.
From Romany F. Mansour, Hesham Alhumyani, Sayed Abdel Khalek, Rashid A. Saeed, and Deepak Gupta. Design of cultural emperor penguin optimizer for energy-efficient resource scheduling in green cloud computing environment. Cluster Computing, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10586-022-03608-0, doi:10.1007/s10586-022-03608-0.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How does the theme of "Green Cluod Computing" connect the discussion of Green IoT with the systematic survey of energy-efficient techniques in sustainabl cloud computing, especially regarding why data centers and cloud technologies are being optimized for lower energy use and reduced environmental harm?

Green Cloud Computing (GCC) provides the common sustainability framework linking Green IoT and energy-efficient cloud computing. In both settings, the core objective is to reduce the power demand of connected computing systems and thereby lower CO2 emissions and broader environmental impacts. For Green IoT, this means conserving energy across massive device, edge, fog, and cloud layers; for cloud computing, it means improving the efficiency of data centers and workloads that support those IoT services. (alsharif2024acomprehensivesurvey chunk 1, bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)

The systematic survey shows that this optimization is driven by the large and growing energy footprint of data centers, computing devices, and networking infrastructure. These systems consume substantial electricity, generate significant heat, and contribute to carbon emissions, so the literature emphasizes techniques such as VM virtualization and consolidation, power-aware scheduling, task offloading, resource shutdown, thermal management, and learning-based control to reduce energy use while preserving service quality. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1, buyya2023energy‐efficiencyandsustainability chunk 1, mansour2022designofcultural chunk 1)

The Green IoT connection is that IoT deployments depend on cloud and edge infrastructure to process data efficiently. Therefore, optimizing cloud technologies is not only a data-center problem but also a prerequisite for sustainable IoT at scale. By making cloud data centers less energy-intensive and less carbon-intensive, GCC supports the sustainability goals of Green IoT and environmentally responsible computing more broadly. (alsharif2024acomprehensivesurvey chunk 1, wang2023reinforcementlearningbased chunk 1, buyya2023energy‐efficiencyandsustainability chunk 1)
